title: bug: claim_next_task still posts the #workers file-collision heads-up on QA REVIEW claims in worktree mode (a mention-less line pages every busy seat), and its claim notice parses mentions out of the task title
description:
This row follows up two QA notes. task-97740aed's reviewSummary says: "QA REVIEW claims open shared attempts so their notices still page". task-85df8bf0's QA lists "the claim notice title" as a site that still echoes agent text.

Evidence at HEAD 119fce99 (packages/moe-daemon/src/tools/claimNextTask.ts):

1. worktreeOnlyCollision (:353) returns false whenever the claimer's attempt is not 'worktree'. Its doc comment deliberately keeps REVIEW and PLANNING claims on the old paging. A QA REVIEW claim opens a shared attempt, so every QA claim of a row whose files overlap a WORKING row posts the #workers heads-up.
   - With no live peer, that line mentions nobody.
   - Outside #general a mention-less system line is not feed (util/chatPayload.ts:54 isSystemFeedMessage). So state/chatStore.ts:196-251 routes it through MentionRouter.routeSystemMessage (util/mentionRouter.ts:255-267) to EVERY busy seat. Each seat gets an unread count and a chat_wait wake.
   - Measured over .moe/messages: 69 collision notices were posted after task-97740aed landed (2026-11-02 22:03Z), and 33 came from qa-* claims. Every QA-claim notice since 02:18Z mentions nobody, so each one paged every busy seat. Examples: 03:14:27Z on fb0ab382, 03:23:49Z on 6d5d3db2, 07:15:47Z on befdddf7, 08:03:36Z on 3acf7f79.
   - In worktree mode a QA seat reviews landed bytes and lands nothing (scripts/CLAUDE.md, Control seats), so the line gives nobody anything to coordinate.

2. :882 posts `${params.workerId} claimed task: ${task.title}` with mention parsing on. task-97740aed's own title contains an at-token ('mentions'). Its three claim notices (2026-11-02 21:41:26Z, 21:51:07Z and 22:01:02Z, all in #general) each recorded mentions ['mentions']. That took them out of the #general feed and routed each one to every busy seat. The fix pattern exists: SystemPostOptions { parseMentions: false } (state/chatStore.ts:394-414), used by completeStep.ts:143 (task-85df8bf0).

Expected behaviour:
- In worktree mode, a REVIEW claim posts no #workers collision heads-up. The response's fileCollision array stays exactly as today. A PLANNING claim that carries a plan should follow the same rule if the planner finds the same reasoning holds.
- The claim notice echoes the title without parsing mentions.
- WORKING claims and shared mode (worktreeMode off) keep today's behaviour.

Files:
- packages/moe-daemon/src/tools/claimNextTask.ts.
- A NEW test file under packages/moe-daemon/src/tools/. Do not edit claimNextTask.test.ts: it is in the open WT-19 row task-b1ca54f2's plan.
- docs/MCP_SERVER.md, the fileCollision paragraph (:1525). It says every claimer that is not in a worktree keeps the heads-up. That file is also in task-f81c85ac's plan (WORKING), so this row dependsOn f81c85ac.
No other open row's plan names claimNextTask.ts (checked at 119fce99).
definitionOfDone: With settings.worktreeMode 'on', a REVIEW claim whose task's affectedFiles overlap a WORKING row posts no #workers file-collision line, and the claim response still returns the same fileCollision entries; with worktreeMode off the same claim still posts as today, and WORKING claims behave as today.
The '<workerId> claimed task: <title>' notice is posted with { parseMentions: false }: a title holding an at-token records mentions [] and routes to no seat; the posted text is unchanged.

A NEW test file under packages/moe-daemon/src/tools/ covers the REVIEW claim in both modes and the at-token title (the at-sign built at runtime, never spelled in source); restoring today's code fails those cases, and claimNextTask.test.ts plus every existing collision test pass unchanged.
docs/MCP_SERVER.md's fileCollision paragraph states the REVIEW-claim rule; no other line of that file changes.
In a snapshot outside the shared checkout: cd packages/moe-daemon && npx vitest run src/tools/claimNextTask.test.ts <new test file> && npx tsc --noEmit exits 0.
